pathways.climate_pressure: Below-average rainfall and drought during the period reviewed in 2022.
pathways.documented_impact: Pastoral households move seasonally in search of grazing and water, including between Namibia and Angola.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Concentration of users and increased pressure on scarce grazing and water resources.
pathways.possible_consequence: IFRC associates this movement with resource competition and conflict, without specifying conflict type, incidents or scale.
institutions: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies
alternative_explanations: Land access, service provision, pre-existing resource arrangements and livelihood conditions also shape competition; mobility is an established risk-management practice.
pathways.uncertainty: Localized qualitative assessment. Conflict is unspecified and must not be read as armed violence, ethnic hostility or a general risk posed by migrants.
resilience_factors: Pastoral mobility can manage climatic risk; water-system rehabilitation and cash assistance were reported separately, without evaluated conflict-prevention outcomes.
pathways.compact_statement: The 2022 IFRC assessment associates drought-related pastoral movement with resource competition and unspecified conflict, not an armed-conflict forecast.

gaps: The IFRC assessment describes both human–wildlife conflict and pastoral mobility associated with resource competition. The latter does not specify conflict type or scale; neither supports an armed-conflict or migrant-threat inference.
No verified conflict-to-adaptation pathway was found. Local evidence is selective, while the 2026 after-action review is retrospective and mostly national.
Historical poverty, food-security and service indicators are not current 2026 prevalence. IPC projection for January–March 2023 was excluded.
Reported aid reach and water-response benefits are assessment findings, not measured lasting recovery or counterfactual impacts.

executive_assessment.text: Named northern and central water-stressed areas face differentiated livelihood, nutrition and service-access constraints, with most local indicators dating to 2015/16–2022.

Pastoral mobility is an established coping strategy. A localized IFRC assessment associates drought-related movement with resource competition and unspecified conflict; human–wildlife conflict is a separate finding.

Finance and insurance access, local response authority, early-action delays and distribution safeguards constrain capacity. Reported historical interventions and 2024/25 response reach do not establish sustained recovery.
